sanskrit: tato vipulam ānāyya devaśarmā mahātapāḥ puṣpārthe codayām āsa gaccha gaccheti bhārata
english: Then, O Bhārata, Devaśarman of great austerity summoned Vipula and urged him on for the sake of the flowers, saying, "Go, go."

sanskrit: vipulas tu guror vākyam avicārya mahātapāḥ sa tathety abravīd rājaṃs taṃ ca deśaṃ jagāma ha
english: And Vipula, of great austerity, without questioning his teacher's word, said "So be it," O king, and went to that region.

sanskrit: yasmin deśe tu tāny āsan patitāni nabhastalāt amlānāny api tatrāsan kusumāny aparāṇy api
english: In the region where those blossoms had fallen from the vault of the sky, other unwithered flowers also lay there.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tāni jagrāha divyāni rucirāṇi ca prāptāni svena tapasā divyagandhāni bhārata
english: Then he gathered up those flowers, celestial and lovely, won by his own austerity and divine in fragrance, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃprāpya tāni prītātmā guror vacanakārakaḥ tato jagāma tūrṇaṃ ca campāṃ campakamālinīm
english: Having obtained them, glad of heart and obedient to his teacher's word, he then swiftly set out for Campā, garlanded with campaka trees.

sanskrit: sa vane vijane tāta dadarśa mithunaṃ nṛṇām cakravat parivartantaṃ gṛhītvā pāṇinā karam
english: In a deserted forest, my son, he saw a pair of beings turning round and round like a wheel, each grasping the other's hand.

sanskrit: tatraikas tūrṇam agamat tatpade parivartayan ekas tu na tathā rājaṃś cakratuḥ kalahaṃ tataḥ
english: There one of them moved swiftly, wheeling about in step, but the other did not do so likewise, O king; and thereupon the two fell to quarrelling.

sanskrit: tvaṃ śīghraṃ gacchasīty eko 'bravīn neti tathāparaḥ neti neti ca tau tāta parasparam athocatuḥ
english: "You go too fast," said the one; "No," said the other; and "No, no!" the two of them, my son, then said to each other.

sanskrit: tayor vispardhator evaṃ śapatho 'yam abhūt tadā manasoddiśya vipulaṃ tato vākyam athocatuḥ
english: As the two thus contended, this oath then arose; fixing their minds upon Vipula, they spoke these words:

sanskrit: āvayor anṛtaṃ prāha yas tasyātha dvijasya vai vipulasya pare loke yā gatiḥ sā bhaved iti
english: "Whichever of us two has spoken falsely, may his lot in the world beyond be that of the brahmin Vipula!"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vipulo viṣaṇṇavadano 'bhavat evaṃ tīvratapāś cāhaṃ kaṣṭaś cāyaṃ parigrahaḥ
english: Hearing this, Vipula grew downcast of face, thinking: "I, of such fierce austerity—and yet this fate they invoke is a grievous burden."

sanskrit: mithunasyāsya kiṃ me syāt kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yato gatiḥ aniṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ kīrtitānena me 'dya vai
english: "What sin of mine toward this pair could there be, that a destiny abhorred by all creatures has today been proclaimed for me by them?"

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintayann eva vipulo rājasattama avāṅmukho nyastaśirā dadhyau duṣkṛtam ātmanaḥ
english: Pondering thus, O best of kings, Vipula, his face downcast and his head bowed, brooded upon his own misdeed.

sanskrit: tataḥ ṣaḍ anyān puruṣān akṣaiḥ kāñcanarājataiḥ apaśyad dīvyamānān vai lobhaharṣānvitāṃs tathā
english: Then he saw six other men gambling with dice of gold and silver, filled with greed and glee.

sanskrit: kurvataḥ śapathaṃ taṃ vai yaḥ kṛto mithunena vai vipulaṃ vai samuddiśya te 'pi vākyam athābruvan
english: As they swore that very oath which the pair had sworn, they too, with Vipula in mind, then spoke these words:

sanskrit: yo lobham āsthāyāsmākaṃ viṣamaṃ kartum utsahet vipulasya pare loke yā gatis tām avāpnuyāt
english: "Whoever among us, yielding to greed, should venture to play foul, may he attain that lot which in the world beyond is Vipula's!"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vipulo nāpaśyad dharmasaṃkaram janmaprabhṛti kauravya kṛtapūrvam athātmanaḥ
english: Hearing this, Vipula could find no breach of dharma committed by himself before, from his very birth onward, O scion of the Kurus.

sanskrit: sa pradadhyau tadā rājann agnāv agnir ivāhitaḥ dahyamānena manasā śāpaṃ śrutvā tathāvidham
english: He brooded then, O king, like fire laid upon fire, his mind consumed with burning at having heard such a curse.

sanskrit: tasya cintayatas tāta bahvyo dinaniśā yayuḥ idam āsīn manasi ca rucyā rakṣaṇakāritam
english: While he brooded, my son, many days and nights passed by; and this lay upon his mind—the guarding he had done in the matter of Ruci.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇenaiva vadanaṃ vadanena ca vidhāya na mayā coktaṃ satyam etad guros tadā
english: "By matching feature with feature and face with face I wrought the deed, and I did not then tell my teacher the truth of it."

sanskrit: etad ātmani kauravya duṣkṛtaṃ vipulas tadā amanyata mahābhāga tathā tac ca na saṃśayaḥ
english: This, O Kaurava, Vipula then reckoned a misdeed in himself, O illustrious one—and so indeed it was, beyond doubt.

sanskrit: sa campāṃ nagarīm etya puṣpāṇi gurave dadau pūjayām āsa ca guruṃ vidhivat sa gurupriyaḥ
english: Reaching the city of Campā, he gave the flowers to his teacher and, dear to his teacher as he was, honored him duly according to rite.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tam āgatam abhiprekṣya śiṣyaṃ vākyam athābravīt devaśarmā mahātejā yat tac chṛṇu narādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: Looking upon his disciple who had returned, Devaśarman of great splendor then spoke these words—hear them, O lord of men.

sanskrit: devaśarmovāca kiṃ te vipula dṛṣṭaṃ vai tasminn adya mahāvane te tvā jānanti nipuṇa ātmā ca rucir eva ca
english: Devaśarman said: What did you see today, Vipula, in that great forest? They know you, O skillful one—your own self too, and Ruci as well.

sanskrit: vipula uvāca brahmarṣe mithunaṃ kiṃ tat ke ca te puruṣā vibho ye māṃ jānanti tattvena tāṃś ca me vaktum arhasi
english: Vipula said: O brahmin-sage, what was that pair, and who were those men, O mighty one, who know me in truth? You ought to tell me of them.

sanskrit: devaśarmovāca yad vai tan mithunaṃ brahmann ahorātraṃ hi viddhi tat cakravat parivarteta tat te jānāti duṣkṛtam
english: Devaśarman said: That pair, O brahmin, know to be day and night; wheeling round like a wheel, they know your misdeed.

sanskrit: ye ca te puruṣā vipra akṣair dīvyanti hṛṣṭavat ṛtūṃs tān abhijānīhi te te jānanti duṣkṛtam
english: And those men, O brahmin, who gamble joyously with dice—know them to be the seasons; they too know your misdeed.

sanskrit: na māṃ kaś cid vijānīta iti kṛtvā na viśvaset naro rahasi pāpātmā pāpakaṃ karma vai dvija
english: Let no man of evil soul trust, thinking "None knows me," when he does a sinful deed in secret, O brahmin.

sanskrit: kurvāṇaṃ hi naraṃ karma pāpaṃ rahasi sarvadā paśyanti ṛtavaś cāpi tathā dinaniśe 'py uta
english: For the seasons forever behold a man doing a sinful deed in secret, and so too do day and night.

sanskrit: te tvāṃ harṣasmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā guroḥ karmānivedakam smārayantas tathā prāhus te yathā śrutavān bhavān
english: Seeing you smiling with joy yet not disclosing your deed to your teacher, they spoke thus to remind you, as you have heard.

sanskrit: ahorātraṃ vijānāti ṛtavaś cāpi nityaśaḥ puruṣe pāpakaṃ karma śubhaṃ vā śubhakarmaṇaḥ
english: Day and night know, and the seasons too know forever, the sinful deed in a man, or the auspicious deed of him who acts auspiciously.

sanskrit: tat tvayā mama yat karma vyabhicārād bhayātmakam nākhyātam iti jānantas te tvām āhus tathā dvija
english: Knowing that you did not declare to me that deed of yours, born of transgression and full of fear, they spoke to you thus, O brahmin.

sanskrit: te caiva hi bhaveyus te lokāḥ pāpakṛto yathā kṛtvā nācakṣataḥ karma mama yac ca tvayā kṛtam
english: And those worlds would befall you, as they befall the doer of sin, had you done that deed of yours and not disclosed it to me.

sanskrit: tathā śakyā ca durvṛttā rakṣituṃ pramadā dvija na ca tvaṃ kṛtavān kiṃ cid āgaḥ prīto 'smi tena te
english: And thus an ill-conducted woman can be guarded, O brahmin; but you committed no offense at all—therein I am pleased with you.

sanskrit: yadi tv ahaṃ tvā durvṛttam adrākṣaṃ dvijasattama śapeyaṃ tvām ahaṃ krodhān na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: But had I seen you ill-conducted, O best of brahmins, I would have cursed you in anger—of that I have no doubt.

sanskrit: sajjanti puruṣe nāryaḥ puṃsāṃ so 'rthaś ca puṣkalaḥ anyathā rakṣataḥ śāpo 'bhaviṣyat te gatiś ca sā
english: Women cling to a man, and great is men's desire for them; had you guarded her otherwise, the curse and that fate would have been yours.

sanskrit: rakṣitā sā tvayā putra mama cāpi niveditā ahaṃ te prītimāṃs tāta svasti svargaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: She was guarded by you, my son, and reported to me as well. I am pleased with you, dear child; blessings upon you—you shall go to heaven.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktvā vipulaṃ prīto devaśarmā mahān ṛṣiḥ mumoda svargam āsthāya sahabhāryaḥ saśiṣyakaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus to Vipula, the pleased and great sage Devaśarman rejoiced, attaining heaven together with his wife and his disciple.

sanskrit: idam ākhyātavāṃś cāpi mamākhyānaṃ mahāmuniḥ mārkaṇḍeyaḥ purā rājan gaṅgākūle kathāntare
english: This tale, O king, the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya once told me long ago, in the course of a discourse on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tasmād bravīmi pārtha tvā striyaḥ sarvāḥ sadaiva ca ubhayaṃ dṛśyate tāsu satataṃ sādhv asādhu ca
english: Therefore I tell you, O Pārtha, concerning all women: in them both are ever to be seen, the good and the bad alike.

sanskrit: striyaḥ sādhvyo mahābhāgāḥ saṃmatā lokamātaraḥ dhārayanti mahīṃ rājann imāṃ savanakānanām
english: Virtuous women, illustrious, esteemed as the mothers of the world, uphold this earth, O king, with its forests and groves.

sanskrit: asādhvyaś cāpi durvṛttāḥ kulaghnyaḥ pāpaniścayāḥ vijñeyā lakṣaṇair duṣṭaiḥ svagātrasahajair nṛpa
english: But the unvirtuous, ill-conducted, ruinous to their families and bent on evil, are to be known by the evil marks inborn in their own bodies, O king.

sanskrit: evam etāsu rakṣā vai śakyā kartuṃ mahātmabhiḥ anyathā rājaśārdūla na śakyā rakṣituṃ striyaḥ
english: Thus by great souls women can be guarded; otherwise, O tiger among kings, women cannot be guarded at all.

sanskrit: etā hi manujavyāghra tīkṣṇās tīkṣṇaparākramāḥ nāsām asti priyo nāma maithune saṃgame nṛbhiḥ
english: For these, O tiger among men, are fierce and of fierce vigor; there is none truly dear to them in union and intercourse with men.

sanskrit: etāḥ kṛtyāś ca kāryāś ca kṛtāś ca bharatarṣabha na caikasmin ramanty etāḥ puruṣe pāṇḍunandana
english: These are to be wooed and to be won and to be possessed, O bull of the Bharatas; yet these find no lasting delight in any single man, O joy of the Pāṇḍus.

sanskrit: nāsu sneho nṛbhiḥ kāryas tathaiverṣyā janeśvara khedam āsthāya bhuñjīta dharmam āsthāya caiva hi
english: No fondness, and likewise no jealousy, should be shown toward them by men, O lord of people; resting in patience and resting in dharma, let a man enjoy his lot.

sanskrit: vihanyetānyathā kurvan naraḥ kauravanandana sarvathā rājaśārdūla yuktiḥ sarvatra pūjyate
english: A man who acts otherwise comes to ruin, O joy of the Kurus; in every case, O tiger among kings, sound judgment is everywhere to be honored.

sanskrit: tenaikena tu rakṣā vai vipulena kṛtā striyāḥ nānyaḥ śakto nṛloke 'smin rakṣituṃ nṛpa yoṣitaḥ
english: By Vipula alone was the guarding of a woman accomplished; no other in this world of men, O king, has been able to guard women.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yan mūlaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ prajanasya gṛhasya ca pitṛdevātithīnāṃ ca tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That which is the root of all duties, of offspring and of the household, and of the rites to ancestors, gods, and guests—of this tell me, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ayaṃ hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmaś cintyatamo mataḥ kīdṛśāya pradeyā syāt kanyeti vasudhādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: This indeed, of all duties, is held the most to be pondered, O lord of the earth—namely, to what kind of man a maiden should be given.

sanskrit: śīlavṛtte samājñāya vidyāṃ yoniṃ ca karma ca adbhir eva pradātavyā kanyā guṇavate vare brāhmaṇānāṃ satām eṣa dharmo nityaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Having well examined his character and conduct, his learning, his lineage, and his deeds, a maiden should be given, with the pouring of water, to a worthy suitor of good qualities. This, O Yudhiṣṭhira, is the eternal duty of righteous brahmins.

sanskrit: āvāhyam āvahed evaṃ yo dadyād anukūlataḥ śiṣṭānāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: He should take in marriage from one fit to give in marriage, and he who gives should give willingly—this is the eternal duty of cultivated kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: ātmābhipretam utsṛjya kanyābhipreta eva yaḥ abhipretā ca yā yasya tasmai deyā yudhiṣṭhira gāndharvam iti taṃ dharmaṃ prāhur dharmavido janāḥ
english: Setting aside his own preference, when a man is the maiden's own choice, and she who is desired by him is given to him, O Yudhiṣṭhira—that rite those versed in dharma call the gāndharva.

sanskrit: dhanena bahunā krītvā saṃpralobhya ca bāndhavān asurāṇāṃ nṛpaitaṃ vai dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Buying her with much wealth and enticing her kinsmen—this, O king, the wise declare to be the rite of the asuras.

sanskrit: hatvā chittvā ca śīrṣāṇi rudatāṃ rudatīṃ gṛhāt prasahya haraṇaṃ tāta rākṣasaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam
english: Slaying and cleaving the heads of those who weep, and carrying off by force the weeping maiden from her home, my son—that is the mark of the rākṣasa rite.

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ tu trayo dharmyā dvāv adharmyau yudhiṣṭhira paiśāca āsuraś caiva na kartavyau kathaṃ cana
english: Of the five, three are lawful and two unlawful, O Yudhiṣṭhira; the paiśāca and the āsura should never be practiced in any way.

sanskrit: brāhmaḥ kṣātro 'tha gāndharva ete dharmyā nararṣabha pṛthag vā yadi vā miśrāḥ kartavyā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The brāhma, the kṣātra, and the gāndharva—these are lawful, O bull among men; whether singly or combined, they may be practiced, herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: tisro bhāryā brāhmaṇasya dve bhārye kṣatriyasya tu vaiśyaḥ svajātiṃ vindeta tāsv apatyaṃ samaṃ bhavet
english: Three wives may a brahmin have, but two wives a kṣatriya; a vaiśya should take a wife of his own caste; among these the offspring rank equal.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇī tu bhavej jyeṣṭhā kṣatriyā kṣatriyasya tu ratyartham api śūdrā syān nety āhur apare janāḥ
english: The brahmin wife should be foremost, and the kṣatriya wife of a kṣatriya; a śūdra wife may be taken for pleasure—though others say, "No."

sanskrit: apatyajanma śūdrāyāṃ na praśaṃsanti sādhavaḥ śūdrāyāṃ janayan vipraḥ prāyaścittī vidhīyate
english: The good do not approve the begetting of offspring upon a śūdra woman; a brahmin who begets children upon a śūdra woman is enjoined to perform expiation.

sanskrit: triṃśadvarṣo daśavarṣāṃ bhāryāṃ vindeta nagnikām ekaviṃśativarṣo vā saptavarṣām avāpnuyāt
english: A man of thirty years should take to wife a girl of ten, still a maiden; or one of twenty-one should win one of seven years.

sanskrit: yasyās tu na bhaved bhrātā pitā vā bharatarṣabha nopayaccheta tāṃ jātu putrikādharmiṇī hi sā
english: But her who has neither brother nor father, O bull of the Bharatas, one should never marry, for she is bound by the law of the appointed daughter.

sanskrit: trīṇi varṣāṇy udīkṣeta kanyā ṛtumatī satī caturthe tv atha saṃprāpte svayaṃ bhartāram arjayet
english: A maiden who has reached her courses should wait three years; but when the fourth has come, she may herself win a husband.

sanskrit: prajano hīyate tasyā ratiś ca bharatarṣabha ato 'nyathā vartamānā bhaved vācyā prajāpateḥ
english: Her chance of offspring is lost, and her pleasure too, O bull of the Bharatas; one who acts otherwise becomes blameworthy before Prajāpati.

sanskrit: asapiṇḍā ca yā mātur asagotrā ca yā pituḥ ity etām anugaccheta taṃ dharmaṃ manur abravīt
english: One who is not a sapiṇḍa of his mother and not of the same gotra as his father—such a one should he take; that law Manu has declared.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śulkam anyena dattaṃ syād dadānīty āha cāparaḥ balād anyaḥ prabhāṣeta dhanam anyaḥ pradarśayet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: One man may have paid the bride-price; another may say, "I shall pay it"; another may speak with force; and another may display his wealth.

sanskrit: pāṇigrahītā tv anyaḥ syāt kasya kanyā pitāmaha tattvaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ cakṣur bhavatu no bhavān
english: And yet another may be the one who takes her hand—whose, then, is the maiden, O grandfather? For us who seek to know the truth, may you be our eye.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yat kiṃ cit karma mānuṣyaṃ saṃsthānāya prakṛṣyate mantravan mantritaṃ tasya mṛṣāvādas tu pātakaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Whatever human act is carried forward to its conclusion, its sealing with sacred words is as with a binding formula; but a false utterance therein is a sin.

sanskrit: bhāryāpatyṛtvigācāryāḥ śiṣyopādhyāya eva ca mṛṣokte daṇḍam arhanti nety āhur apare janāḥ
english: Wife, offspring, officiating priest, and teacher, and disciple and instructor too, deserve punishment when falsely addressed—though others say, "No."

sanskrit: na hy akāmena saṃvādaṃ manur evaṃ praśaṃsati ayaśasyam adharmyaṃ ca yan mṛṣā dharmakopanam
english: For Manu does not commend an agreement made unwillingly; what is false is inglorious and unlawful and provokes the wrath of dharma.

sanskrit: naikāntadoṣa ekasmiṃs tad dānaṃ nopalabhyate dharmato yāṃ prayacchanti yāṃ ca krīṇanti bhārata
english: There is no fault wholly fixed upon any one man, where such a gift is not properly obtained—she whom they bestow according to dharma, and she whom they buy, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bandhubhiḥ samanujñāto mantrahomau prayojayet tathā sidhyanti te mantrā nādattāyāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: With the kinsmen's consent, let him perform the sacred words and the oblation; thus those formulas avail—never in the case of one not duly given.

sanskrit: yas tv atra mantrasamayo bhāryāpatyor mithaḥ kṛtaḥ tam evāhur garīyāṃsaṃ yaś cāsau jñātibhiḥ kṛtaḥ
english: That compact of sacred words which is made mutually between wife and husband—that, and the one made with the kinsmen, they declare the weightier.

sanskrit: devadattāṃ patir bhāryāṃ vetti dharmasya śāsanāt sā daivīṃ mānuṣīṃ vācam anṛtāṃ paryudasyati
english: By the ordinance of dharma a husband knows his wife as given by the gods; she casts off as false all other speech, divine or human.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kanyāyāṃ prāptaśulkāyāṃ jyāyāṃś ced āvrajed varaḥ dharmakāmārthasaṃpanno vācyam atrānṛtaṃ na vā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a maiden's bride-price has been received, if a better suitor should come, endowed with dharma, desire, and wealth—should an untruth be spoken here, or not?

sanskrit: tasminn ubhayato doṣe kurvañ chreyaḥ samācaret ayaṃ naḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmaś cintyatamo mataḥ
english: When fault lies on both sides in that matter, let a man do and practice the better course. This, of all our duties, we hold the most to be pondered.

sanskrit: tattvaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ cakṣur bhavatu no bhavān tad etat sarvam ācakṣva na hi tṛpyāmi kathyatām
english: For us who seek to know the truth, may you be our eye; tell us all of this, for I am not sated—let it be told.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na vai niṣṭhākaraṃ śulkaṃ jñātvāsīt tena nāhṛtam na hi śulkaparāḥ santaḥ kanyāṃ dadati karhi cit
english: Bhīṣma said: Knowing that bride-price is not what makes the marriage final, no good man ever exacted it; for the good, intent on a bride-price, never give a maiden at all.

sanskrit: anyair guṇair upetaṃ tu śulkaṃ yācanti bāndhavāḥ alaṃkṛtvā vahasveti yo dadyād anukūlataḥ
english: But the kinsmen ask, as it were, a bride-price consisting of other good qualities—"Adorn her and take her away," says he who gives willingly.

sanskrit: tac ca tāṃ ca dadāty eva na śulkaṃ vikrayo na saḥ pratigṛhya bhaved deyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: He gives both that gift and her as well; it is no bride-price, and that is no sale. What is received in turn should be given back—this is the eternal law.
